name: Pierogi Ruskie (Homemade)
summary: Homemade dumplings filled with potato, cheese, and onion, boiled then topped with fried onions in butter and sour cream. About ten each.

ingredients.name: yellow onions, finely diced (one for the filling, one for the topping)

instructions: Dough: mix the flour, egg, oil, 1 tsp salt, and about 200 mL warm water into a soft dough. Knead 5 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest 30 minutes. Put the cottage cheese in a sieve to drain while it rests.

Filling: boil the potatoes 15 minutes until soft and drain well. Fry one onion in 1 tbsp butter until golden. Mash the potatoes with the fried onion, drained cottage cheese, 1 tsp salt, and plenty of pepper. Let it cool.
Roll the dough thin (2 mm) on a floured counter and cut 7–8 cm circles. Put a heaped teaspoon of filling on each, fold in half, and pinch the edges firmly shut. Re-roll the scraps.
Boil the pierogi in batches in salted water. Once they float, cook 2 minutes more and lift out with a slotted spoon.
Fry the second onion in the rest of the butter until golden, spoon over the pierogi, and serve with sour cream.

substitutions.substitute: gluten-free all-purpose flour blend with xanthan gum, plus 1 extra egg. The dough is more fragile, so roll it a little thicker
substitutions.costNote: GF flour blend is about $6–$7/kg (estimate), adding about $2.50; total about $10.60

glutenFree.notes: The potato, cheese, and onion filling is naturally gluten-free. The wheat-flour dough is the only source of gluten.

budgetNotes: Substitution: drained cottage cheese replaces twaróg, the dry Polish farmer's cheese that isn't sold at most chain grocers. The taste changes: twaróg is drier, tangier, and crumbly, so the filling tastes sharper and holds together firmly. Cottage cheese is milder and wetter. Drain it well in a sieve and press out the liquid, or the filling goes soft. If you find twaróg or pressed cottage cheese at a Polish or European deli, use 250 g the same way.
This takes about an hour, but four people get about 40 pierogi for $8.09. Frozen ones cost about the same and aren't as good.
Freeze extras uncooked on a tray, then bag them. Boil from frozen and add 2 minutes.
